evals.prompt: Build a landing page for a project management SaaS called MilestoneMania. Give it that classic 2010s web design look — you know, like the polished corporate sites from around 2011. Full page with header, hero, features, and footer.
evals.expected_output: A complete HTML page with authentic 2010s aesthetic: dark gradient header, bold uppercase condensed headings, glossy CTA buttons with a top-half shine, alternating white/light-gray section bands, drop shadows on cards and nav, skeuomorphic-style feature icons, fluid layout with generous side padding.
expectations: An HTML file is produced with a complete page structure
The header/nav uses a dark gradient background (linear-gradient or similar — not a flat color)
At least one button has a glossy effect implemented with a ::after pseudo-element or translucent overlay on the top half
The page includes all four requested sections: header/nav, hero, features strip, and footer
A condensed or display font (e.g. Oswald, Bebas Neue, Anton) is loaded and applied to headings
Section backgrounds alternate — at least one section uses a light gray background, another uses white
Drop shadows (box-shadow) appear on navigation, cards, or buttons
Heading text is uppercased via CSS text-transform, not hardcoded as all-caps in the HTML

evals.prompt: I'm building a retro-style website for my email marketing tool, SpamCannon. Can you create a pricing page with three plans: Basic ($19/mo), Business ($49/mo), and Agency ($99/mo)? Make it feel like a proper Web 2.0 site from back in the day.
evals.expected_output: Full pricing page with 2010s Web 2.0 aesthetic: gradient header with nav, bold accent-colored section heading, pricing cards with drop shadows and borders, glossy CTA buttons on each plan, dark footer. Brand palette derived from the product context.
expectations: An HTML file is produced
All three pricing tiers are present with correct names and prices: Basic at $19/mo, Business at $49/mo, Agency at $99/mo
Pricing cards have visible drop shadows (box-shadow on the card elements)
Each pricing card has a CTA button with a glossy or raised visual treatment
The header uses a gradient background rather than a flat color
The color palette feels specific to an email marketing product — not generic gray/blue defaults that could belong to any SaaS

evals.prompt: Can you make me a hero section for my personal finance app, BrokeNoMore? I want it to look like those old glossy sites from back when the iPhone first came out — shiny buttons, that whole thing. Just the hero, not the full page.
evals.expected_output: A standalone hero section (not a full page) with early-2010s aesthetic: dark gradient background or bold accent band, large bold headline, glossy CTA button, a product screenshot or device mockup placeholder. Scoped to the hero component only.
expectations: An HTML/CSS snippet or file is produced
The output is scoped to a hero section — not a full multi-section page
The hero has a glossy CTA button with a raised or shiny visual treatment
The hero uses a gradient or strongly styled background (not plain white/flat)
A product mockup, device frame, or screenshot placeholder is included in the hero
The era is correctly interpreted from the implicit signal ('back when the iPhone first came out') — the output does not look like flat/modern design

evals.prompt: Build a website homepage for a boutique law firm called Billable & Partners LLP. Should feel polished and professional — think early 2010s corporate web, the kind of site a proper firm would have had. Include a nav, a bold intro section, a services list, and a contact CTA at the bottom.
evals.expected_output: A complete homepage with 2010s corporate aesthetic adapted for a non-tech brand: dark navy or charcoal gradient header, conservative but polished typography, services section with icon-heading-body triads, glossy contact CTA button, dark footer. Palette reflects a law firm — not SaaS-style teal or lime green.
expectations: An HTML file is produced with a complete page
The palette is appropriate for a law firm — conservative tones like navy, charcoal, deep burgundy, or dark slate rather than vibrant tech colors
The header uses a dark gradient rather than a flat color
A services section is present with at least 3 service items
A contact CTA section appears near the bottom of the page
Glossy or raised button styling is present on at least one CTA
The overall aesthetic reads as 2010s-era without feeling like a parody or over-the-top retro

evals.prompt: Create a sign-up page for a cloud storage service called DropBucket. The company uses a deep teal and orange color scheme. Make it look like a legit 2012-era SaaS.
evals.expected_output: A sign-up page with 2010s SaaS aesthetic: gradient header in deep teal, a centered sign-up form that looks recessed/inset into the surface, orange glossy submit button, drop shadows throughout. The provided teal/orange palette is honored while maintaining all era-specific chrome.
expectations: An HTML file is produced
The provided color scheme (deep teal and orange) is visibly used — teal in the header/primary areas, orange on CTA/buttons
The sign-up form inputs appear visually inset or recessed (inset box-shadow on inputs)
The submit/CTA button has a glossy or raised effect using the orange brand color
The header uses a gradient (not flat teal)
The page feels like a complete, standalone sign-up page — not just a form dropped on a blank background
